newsitem.title: LEBANON: Most Beirut shares end week up in smaller trade.
newsitem.headline: Most Beirut shares end week up in smaller trade.

text.p: Most active shares rose on the Beirut Stock Exchange in the week ended Thursday despite a 40 percent drop in turnover.
The LIBX bank index rose 2.16 percent to 193.35. The LISPI general index rose 0.63 percent to 96.87 and the BLOM general index rose 2.01 percent to 1,113.27.
However, market turnover fell 40 percent to 663,053 shares in the holiday-shortened week from 1,098,778 a week earlier for a value of $6,770,900 against $13,568,706.
"It is not unusual to have quiet trade in August when people are on vacation," a broker said.
"I think we will see bigger volumes as of September and I expect Solidere to be the star then," the broker added.
Solidere shares, regarded by most bankers as the most undervalued stocks on the market, rose in heavy demand.
Solidere A shares rose 2.9 percent to $13 from $12.625 and B shares rose 1.9 percent to $13.125 from $12.875 last Friday.
Financial markets will close on Friday for the Assumption Day public and market holiday.
On the London Stock Exchange, Solidere's global depositary receipts traded at last Friday's level of $17.3.
Of the listed banks, Banque Audi retreated while the two others made gains.
Banque Audi dropped to $27.125 from $27.25. Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose to $21 from $20.75. Bank of Beirut rose to $5.75 from $5.5 at the end of last week.

Of the four listed industrial firms, Ciments Libanais was steady at $1.2813. Pipemaker Eternit was also unchanged at $1.906. Ciments Blancs fell to $4 from $4.125 when they were last traded on June 20.
There was no trade in tilemaker Uniceramic.
